title: A heavier orbiting object
hook: Change orbiting mass and predict orbital-energy magnitude.
misconception: orbital-energy magnitude stays fixed when orbiting mass doubles.
objective: Apply energy magnitude = GMm/(2r) to compare orbital-energy magnitude when orbiting mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a circular Newtonian orbit with fixed radius around a fixed dominant mass, energy magnitude = GMm/(2r). When orbiting mass doubles, orbital-energy magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model energy magnitude = GMm/(2r); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a circular Newtonian orbit with fixed radius around a fixed dominant mass, with a nonzero initial result. If orbiting mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on orbital-energy magnitude?
recall.why: Apply energy magnitude = GMm/(2r) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
